# OpenSSL-written at-rest fixtures (cross-impl interop)

These three files were generated by the **OpenSSL-backed** `mls` build
(commit `c971692e`, before the pure-Rust migration) so the new RustCrypto
at-rest path can be proven to still open files written by the old OpenSSL path.

Generated with:

```
NK_PASSPHRASE="fixture-pass-123" nk-crypto-tool \
  --mls-cmd create-group --mls-name fixturegroup \
  --mls-storage <dir>/groups.db --transport iroh
```

| File            | Format                                                        |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `at-rest.key`   | `NKCT-AR1`, ver 0x01, KDF 0x01 = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 @ 256000 iters, AES-256-GCM envelope (hybrid SK‖PK) |
| `groups.db.kek` | `NKCT-KEK`, ver 0x02 (bound), suite 0x02 (X-Wing + HKDF-SHA512 + AES-256-GCM); HPKE-sealed DEK, info bound to binding `groups.db` |
| `groups.db`     | SQLCipher DB encrypted with the DEK                            |

Facts the interop test relies on (do not change these files):
- Passphrase: `fixture-pass-123`
- KEK binding: the DB file name `groups.db` (so the test must place the DB at a path whose file name is `groups.db`)
- Group id created: `24664478cc0ac450cb8ae5d7878fd0601bc5de49569f5945d348ed64408b8719`

The interop test copies these into a temp dir, opens `at-rest.key` with the
passphrase, decapsulates the KEK to recover the DEK, and opens `groups.db` —
all with the pure-Rust code. If the RustCrypto PBKDF2/AES-GCM/HPKE bytes ever
diverge from the standards, this test fails.
